recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Body: Kyle and Serena Denton are community herbalists creating wild-crafted and organic plant medicines out of Milwaukee since 2015. I have used their teas and tinctures on an almost daily basis for years now. Kyle is a great friend of InnerVerse and has appeared on the channel more times than I can count. These products work, not in the allopathic "pharma-medicine" way, but in a terrain-support, consciousness bolstering plant-teacher sort of way.
recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Name: Tippecanoe Herbs
recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Offer Line: Use coupon code "innerverse" at checkout for a 10% discount!

recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.
recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Name: The Sonic Slider

recFdBmTf1pJJOP6S.Body: LotusWei provides amazing and transformative plant essence elixirs, using one of nature's most gentle and beautiful elements: the flowers themselves. Led by founder Katie Hess, LotusWei supports customers with diverse products that operate on homeopathic principles and energetic resonances. I use LotusWei Elixirs to give me an edge with psychic & energetic sensitivity, discernment, and life force coherence. In other words, LotusWei Elixirs help me be a better podcaster and Biofield Tuner. Benefits accumulate over long term use!
recFdBmTf1pJJOP6S.Name: LotusWei Flower Elixirs
recFdBmTf1pJJOP6S.Offer Line: Use my affiliate link to support InnerVerse

He has appeared on InnerVerse multiple times to talk about hydrogen as a macronutrient and EZ water.
recIZOksQw0qqj7L0.Name: AquaCure AC50

recMVdJjP2VZJyI2m.Body: Clive de Carle has spent decades researching high-quality natural health essentials, from magnesium and fulvic minerals to iodine, selenium, and vegan-sourced vitamin D. His supplements are formulated with a focus on bioavailability, so the body can actually absorb and use what you're taking rather than letting it pass through unused. It's a simple, no-nonsense approach to filling the nutritional gaps most modern diets leave behind.
recMVdJjP2VZJyI2m.Name: Clive de Carle

rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Name: Chance Garton
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Role: Host of the Innerverse Podcast, biofield tuning practitioner & researcher

recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Bio: Gabriel, known on air as Slick Dissident, co-hosts InnerVerse's Vibe Rant show and is a longtime recurring guest on the podcast. He teaches occult symbolism and tarot on his YouTube channel, ranging across the Major Arcana, the esoteric Enneagram, mythology and archetype, mystic linguistics, and the symbolism hidden in popular film. He is best known for Tarot-tories, his own system mapping the 22 Major Arcana and zodiac archetypes onto the geography of the United States.
recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Name: Gabe (Slick Dissident)
recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Role: Co-host of Vibe Rant; teacher of occult symbolism & tarot

recQOLj1bGHrs7YCW.Bio: Michelle Lundquist describes herself as a folk herbalist, gardener and homemaker with a passion for plants and their ability to heal. She has studied and actively worked with herbs since 2013, drawing most of her knowledge from hands on experience and mentors of the wise woman tradition, and a do it yourself spirit runs through her work as she encourages people to take their wellbeing into their own hands. She hosted more than eighty episodes of The Healing Home podcast as a kitchen witch, homemaker and folk herbalist, and now co-hosts Symbolic Studies with her husband Mario Garza.
recQOLj1bGHrs7YCW.Name: Michelle Lundquist

recbqsYSV8FGvCA28.Bio: Kyle Denton is a community herbalist and medicine maker from Wisconsin who founded Tippecanoe Herbs with his wife Serena Marinelli in 2015. From their Milwaukee apothecary they craft small batch remedies from locally harvested and organic herbs, working from a bio terrain philosophy that blends Ayurveda with Western herbalism. He also runs Root Radical Herbal Academy, has taught for over a decade through his annual three season class and his Milwaukee herb walks, and sees clients as the Tuning Herbalist, using tuning forks to read the biofield. His Substack and podcast, Resonature, explore the interval between vital herbalism, biofield tuning and cosmology.
recbqsYSV8FGvCA28.Name: Kyle Denton
recbqsYSV8FGvCA28.Role: Community herbalist, founder of Tippecanoe Herbs

reckIvJxU4wRhybxA.Bio: Mario Garza is the artist and researcher behind Symbolic Studies, a project sharing symbolic insights on the zodiac, mythology, folklore and world religions, with astrology as its foundation. A lifelong artist who has worked as an art director and graphic designer for nearly 25 years, he runs Symbolic Studies from the Pacific Northwest alongside his wife Michelle, who co-hosts the podcast with him. His work traces syncretic threads across tarot, occultism and comparative religion, including the argument that the major deities of antiquity were originally polar gods before a solar model was laid over them. He also offers symbolic birth chart and tarot readings, private lessons and freelance design.
reckIvJxU4wRhybxA.Name: Mario Garza

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Moon Card and Pisces Gateways", "body": "The panel opened with the Moon card as the Pisces card, and one panelist described its two towers as a gateway, the Hebrew letter Qoph as the back of the head, and the crescent as a vessel. Mario said the ape corresponds with Mercury and pointed to Hanuman and mercurial glyphs on the Thoth card. Gabe described the star Arcturus in Bootes, opposite Pisces, as a great horn like a shofar that marks a new cycle and the lunar calendar. Chance said he was a March 22 Aries, sidereal Pisces, and named escapism into fictional realms as his biggest vice."}, {"title": "Plantain and Valerian Under the Feet", "body": "Kyle described plantain as a stepped on garden weed that grew where people walked, linking its name to the Latin planta of the foot. He said he taught students to chew it onto insect bites and called that his plantain guarantee, and he suggested a liniment as another preparation. Michelle said her first use of it was an oil and wound salve. She then presented valerian as an herb of witches tied to protection and cats, and cautioned that it could stimulate some people instead of calming them. Kyle added that its acrid smell suggested a sedative nature."}, {"title": "Blue Lotus, the Ark and Dreams", "body": "Kyle said he drank and smoked blue lotus while doing his homework the night before, and described vivid dreams and a sense of his third eye pushing outward. A panelist traced the lotus to the Egyptian creation myth and read it as an ark symbol. Chance suggested that anxiety was a lack of imagination because fear narrowed reality to one outcome. Kyle said his supply was a gift and that he was considering an Egyptian supplier. Later a panelist tied the Empress card to Cassiopeia and the Lotus Eaters of the Odyssey."}, {"title": "Mugwort, Artemis and the Gruit Story", "body": "Michelle described mugwort as a dream ally and a crone, and connected it to Artemis, Frigg and Diana. She said she made an infused oil from it and mentioned moxibustion, and she described three species grown on her property. Kyle called mugwort a possible headliner for several signs and told the story of the Bavarian purity law of 1516, saying alewives once brewed with wild herbs before hops took over. He said he preferred wild botanical ferments, and a panelist added that every plant in our surroundings shifted consciousness in some way."}, {"title": "Sea Moss, Echinacea and Usnea", "body": "Kyle said sea moss was the best selling botanical at his shop and called it a red algae that herbalists used as a plant, structuring water in the body. For echinacea, he described an electric tingle on the tongue, followed the plant's energy through the seasons, and compared it to a battle horn for soldiers beside sea moss as a stone mason. Gabe linked its name to the Echidna of myth. Michelle presented usnea as old man's beard and lungs of the forest, harvested ethically after windstorms, and shared a dream calling it guardian of the forest ether."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: It's time to get our feet on the ground as we March towards the vernal equinox, with our resident doctors of the astrological signatures in the plant domain. Our returning wisdom council for part 5 of this zodiacal exploration are Michelle Lundquist of Michelle's Healing Home, Kyle Denton of Tippecanoe Herbs, and Mario Garza of Symbolic Studies.
fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "Pisces is very near and dear to me. I am a March 22 Aries, so in a sidereal sense I'm full on Pisces, but that's right on the cusp. I have a lot of the traits for sure. My biggest vice in life has always been escapism into fictional realms. That's super Piscean.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "It's almost like an indicator of how anxiety is really a lack of imagination because fear is in a way you're just condensing what you expect out of reality down to one outcome that you're like, it has to be like this. And if it's any other way, it won't be OK. But with imagination, you can start to see how every outcome of reality is actually OK.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "I feel like the luckiest podcast host in the world to get to have this wisdom panel teaching me something that I have a lot to learn about and can appreciate the value of the playlist of these astro herbalism talks we've done for the rest of my life. I'll always be able to fall back on this as a reference.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Oh man, am I a big old fan of this garden weed. It's one of the most stepped on plants ever. It's everywhere. We have plantago. We have the planta of the feet. Where the planta go, the plantago grow.", "author": "Kyle Denton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/3bfe296c-3dcd-4af6-bc2e-26466a87ec04/KYLE-DENTON.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "I always tell my students and people I'm on walks with, I give you the plantain guarantee. I put on my car salesman hat and I said, you chew this bad boy up and slap it on your mosquito bite. And I guarantee you that tomorrow it won't itch.", "author": "Kyle Denton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/3bfe296c-3dcd-4af6-bc2e-26466a87ec04/KYLE-DENTON.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "Back before 1516 in Bavaria and surrounding areas, there was an occupation called alewife, and an alewife was a wise woman that would go out into the field and gather some of the herbs of the field and make a fermented brew.", "author": "Kyle Denton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/3bfe296c-3dcd-4af6-bc2e-26466a87ec04/KYLE-DENTON.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "I think one of the things that mugwort does really, really well is that it can help you tap in deeply to things that you may have thought you've already maybe resolved or gone through. Maybe you've concluded, and mugwort has this way of kind of resurfacing some of these things, particularly through the dream realm.", "author": "Michelle Lundquist", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/bff9a941-de38-45a1-a6e9-4e4dcece050e/MICHELLE-LUNDQUIST.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "Instead of seeking something outside of yourself to help you heal or bring you to the next level or whatever, the poppy flower essence is really going to help you to kind of remember who you are and bring you into yourself again. And kind of empower you to just know that you have all this stuff inside of you already.", "author": "Michelle Lundquist", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/bff9a941-de38-45a1-a6e9-4e4dcece050e/MICHELLE-LUNDQUIST.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "Last night, well, probably early this morning, I had a dream and I saw a tree and there was a huge piece of Usnea hanging from it. And the message I got from the dream was that he said he's the guardian of the forest ether.", "author": "Michelle Lundquist", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/bff9a941-de38-45a1-a6e9-4e4dcece050e/MICHELLE-LUNDQUIST.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "The alchemical triangular symbol for water looks like a vessel, right? It looks like you can hold something in there. And then the circular symbol has this horizontal line through it, which reminds me of the whole principle of water always being flat and seeking a level.", "author": "Mario Garza", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/94a2fe35-cc60-4591-8931-7e2b7af18c82/MARIO-GARZA.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "The other thing I'll say regarding ape is that the ape corresponds with Mercury. And so in some magician cards you will see an ape, and the ape in the Vedic tradition is Hanuman, who is the mercurial figure of the pantheon, one of them.", "author": "Mario Garza", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/94a2fe35-cc60-4591-8931-7e2b7af18c82/MARIO-GARZA.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "And this great horn is much like a shofar initiating a new cycle, a new beginning, and it marks the beginning of the lunar calendar. And so all of this really blows my mind because I've always said that it's over here in March, which is the old pagan new year.", "author": "Gabe (Slick Dissident)", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/794d3a0b-c42b-4791-84c3-f79eff430f4c/SLICK-DISSIDENT.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "I consider this also a Piscean card. It's the Empress card, and this is on the Thoth deck. And this one is unique. I like it because her feet are veiled. They're hidden behind the shield. She kind of looks like she could be a mermaid, don't you think?", "author": "Gabe (Slick Dissident)", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/794d3a0b-c42b-4791-84c3-f79eff430f4c/SLICK-DISSIDENT.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}]
